The Nigeria inspection market

Nigeria's NDT market is one of Africa's largest — NNPC, Shell SPDC, Chevron Nigeria, ExxonMobil Nigeria (offshore), TotalEnergies Nigeria, Eni / Agip Nigeria, the new Dangote Refinery (650,000 bpd Lekki — Africa's largest), and the long-troubled Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna NNPC refineries currently undergoing rehabilitation.

Certifications most in demand in Nigeria

Primary: ASNT. Secondary: ISO 9712. Also frequently requested: PCN, CSWIP.

What drives NDT training demand in Nigeria

Nigeria's inspection demand centres on the Niger Delta — offshore platforms and FPSOs, an ageing pipeline network under constant integrity pressure, and the Dangote refinery, which added a world-scale process complex to Lagos overnight. Every one of those assets is examined on intervals set by code, and the examinations must be performed by certified personnel — which is what creates continuous local demand for qualified technicians, and continuous pressure on employers to develop them.

Which methods to train first in this market

Training investment should follow the local work. In Nigeria that means UT structural and topside work, MT for fatigue-driven weld examination, and eddy current/ACFM through coatings; in the pipeline sector, RT to API 1104, AUT/PAUT for girth welds, and MT at dig sites; and where refining work features, UT thickness and corrosion monitoring, phased array on welds, and API-track inspection knowledge. A candidate who certifies against what local employers actually examine is employable months sooner than one who spreads across every method thinly.

Which certification scheme employers here expect

NUPRC and NMDPRA oversight frames oil and gas work, operators run their own stringent vendor approval, local-content rules under NOGICD shape crew composition, and security planning is part of every field mobilisation in a way it is not elsewhere.

For a candidate this decides the route before any course is booked: train toward the scheme your target employers name in their contracts. Where both employer-based (SNT-TC-1A) and central (ISO 9712 / PCN) certification circulate, the central certificate travels with you between employers — worth weighing against the faster employer-based route. How ASNT certification works · ISO 9712 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Levels, honestly explained

Level I performs calibrations and examinations under supervision — the entry point, usually reached in one method first. Level II sets up, interprets against the code and signs the report; it is the level contracts in Nigeria actually specify. Level III writes and approves procedures and qualifies the Level I/IIs — the level a growing inspection function eventually needs to own or engage. Progression is training hours plus documented experience hours, so anyone already working under supervision moves faster than a cold start.
